sentences.text:
National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Kalawati Bai & 6 Others on 9 July,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:24671
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 2 nd Of September, 20
 Misc. Appeal No. 2448 of 2
 National Insurance Co.Ltd.
 Versus
 Kalawati Bai & 6 Others And Others

Appearance:
 Shri Sudhir Dhandwate - Advocate for the appellant  Shri Vijay Singh Chouhan, learned counsel for the   7].
 Shri R.N.Dave - Advocate with Shri Hemant Vaishnav  the respondents.

HEARD ON: 
 DELIVERED ON: 02

O The appellant/Insurance Company has filed this appeal being aggrieved by the award dated 18.05.2007 passed in Claim Case No.206/2005 challenging the liability of the insurance company inter alia on the ground that in fact the owner of the vehicle himself was the driver and there was complete absence of negligence, the accident occurred due to motorcycle lost its balance, as such,
the insurance company cannot be saddled with the liability of payment of insurance.

The second ground is that the two unmarried daughters who were Claimant Nos. 5 and 6, were made party NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24671 2 MA-2448-2007 pursuant to the order of the claims tribunal itself though they were not dependent on the deceased.

2. Short facts of the case are that the deceased Parwatibai Yadav was going as a pillion rider on 15.08.2005 at around 8:30 in the night on the motorcycle having Registration No.MP-09-LF-4846 from MY Hospital to Palasiya.

The said motorcycle was being ridden by the respondent No.1- Deepak in rash and negligent manner, the same got dis-balanced due to rash and negligent riding of the respondent no. 1 and dashed into the divider of the road because of which Parwatibai fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
She was immediately rushed to the hospital where she died during treatment.
Initially, her sister claimant No.1 Kalawati and Kalawati's three children filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act before the claims tribunal.

The claims tribunal vide order dated 10.11.2006 directed the claimant No.1 to implead two married daughters and son National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Kalawati Bai & 6 Others on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22102234/
1 as party in the claim petition.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Kalawati Bai & 6 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Pursuant to which, an application was filed by the claimant No.1 and the claims tribunal vide order dated 09.01.2007 permitted impleadment of both the daughters of the deceased Parwatibai as claimants.
The son of the deceased Deepak was already impleaded as respondent No.1 for the reasons that he was the rider, who was riding the bike when the accident occurred.

3. The claims tribunal after considering the evidence available on record concluded that the claimant No.1 Kalawati being a married sister living separately and her three children i.e. claimant No.2 to 4 were not dependent on deceased Parwatibai.

As such, the claims tribunal in para 17 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24671 3 MA-2448-2007 concluded that the claimants No.1 to 4 are not dependent and are also not their legal heirs thus, they are not entitled for any compensation.

4. However, the claims tribunal after denying compensation to claimant Nos.1 to 4, went on to held that two daughters i.e. claimants Nos.5 and 6 as well as non-applicant No.1 Deepak, being the daughters and son of the deceased are legal heirs of the deceased hence, they are entitle for the compensation.
5.

After concluding thus, the claims tribunal recorded the findings regarding income of the deceased which was taken at Rs. 1,21,236/- per annum and after deducting 1/3rd from the same for personal expenses of the deceased, compensation of Rs. 8,86,064/- was directed to be paid to the claimants No.5 and 6 and non-applicant No.1.
6. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company points out that initially only claimants No.1 to 4 filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act.
It was only on the order of the claims tribunal that the daughters were impleaded as claimant Nos.5 and 6.

He submits that even after their impleadment, they never turned up before the claims tribunal, neither they filed any claim nor deposed before the tribunal establishing their dependency on the deceased Parwatibai.
He submits that married daughters, unless established otherwise, cannot be treated as dependents on the income of their mother.

In support of his submission he places reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in the case of Deep Shikha & Another vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. &
Ors 2025 SCC OnLine SC 1090.

entities.text:
Deep Shikha & Another vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. &
Ors 2025 SCC OnLine SC 1090
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that in absence of proving dependency, the inclusion of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24671 4 MA-2448-2007 two daughters as dependent and consequently making deduction at 1/3rd is also not correct.
In view of the fact that if the two daughters are excluded then only one dependent remains i.e. the son of the deceased, hence, the deduction would be only at the rate of 50%.

7. He further submits that in any case the insurance company could not have been made liable for payment of compensation in view of the fact that in fact there was no proof of rash and negligent driving, there was initial report that the vehicle got dis-balanced and rammed into the divider but subsequently this story before the claims tribunal was improved by inserting the ingredient of rash and negligent driving.
He thus submits that the award of compensation even on this count is not sustainable.

He also points out that in fact, the perpetrator of the act i.e. respondent no. 1 will get benefited for his act if his claim is entertained, because he was the person who is responsible for the National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Kalawati Bai & 6 Others on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22102234/
2 accident.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Kalawati Bai & 6 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further states that pillion rider was not covered under the policy.
Hence, he prays for setting aside the impugned award.
8. Per contra, learned counsel for the claimants refers to para 9 of the claim petition and submits that there was a clear pleading of negligence which even the tribunal has found proved.

As regards the award of compensation to two daughters, he submits that indisputably the two daughters are legal representative of the deceased as such irrespective of any dependency they represents the estate of the deceased.
Hence, the claims tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation to all the three children.
With respect to the contention of the Insurance Company that the pillion rider was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24671 5 MA-2448-2007 not covered under the policy.
It has been submitted that the insurance policy was a comprehensive policy thus, even the pillion rider was covered in the same.

In support of his submission, he relied on the judgments passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in the case of Krishna Bus Service Ltd. vs. Smt. Mangli and Others reported in 1976 A.C.J. 184 as well as in the case of Indra Purushottam Rajak vs. Dayaram and Others reported in 2017 ACJ 2512.
9.

entities.text: Krishna Bus Service Ltd. vs. Smt. Mangli and Others reported in 1976 A.C.J. 184
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Indra Purushottam Rajak vs. Dayaram and Others reported in 2017 ACJ 2512
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that it is immaterial for the purposes of the compensation that the person driving the vehicle gets compensation this will not amount to giving benefit of his own fault.

10. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
11.
As can be seen from the proceedings before the claims tribunal, initially there were only four claimants i.e. sister of the deceased and sister's three children.
The claims tribunal when found that there are two daughters and one son of the deceased, it directed the original claimants to implead them as party.
It appears the Tribunal directed for the same in view of the provisions of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act.
In the present case, the tribunal directed the original claimants should implead the married sisters as party to the application, thus they were made claimants No.5 and 6.

However, they never turned up before the Tribunal for establishing their dependency and it is for this reason that the tribunal is of the view that the two married daughters were never interested in the claim proceedings as they never turned up before the tribunal.
The requirement of Section 166 is that the application shall be made on behalf of both benefit of all the LRs of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24671 6 MA-2448-2007 deceased
however, it also says that those LRs who have not joined shall be impleaded as respondents to the application.
In the present case as it is apparent that two daughters were never interested to join, they should have been made respondents.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Deep Shikha (supra) has considered the aspect of dependency of married daughter in para 13 and 14, in which the Hon'ble Court observed as under:-
"13.
Once a daughter is married, logical presumption is that she now has rights on her matrimonial household and is also financially supported by her husband or his family, unless proven otherwise.
It is more than likely that her dependence on her natal family, including her mother has now ceased.
Sections 166 and 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 focus on the financial relationship between the deceased and the Claimant.

A married daughter may be considered a legal representative, as per National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Kalawati Bai & 6 Others on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22102234/
3 Manjuri Bera, but she will not be eligible for loss of dependency compensation unless it is proven by the daughter that she was financially dependent on the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Kalawati Bai & 6 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is clear from the record that Appellant No. 1 has failed to prove that she was being financially supported by her mother post marriage and hence cannot be said to be a dependent of her mother, the deceased.

14. Therefore, it is our opinion the High Court correctly relied on Manjuri Bera while holding that Appellant No.1, as the legal representative of the deceased, will only be entitled to compensation envisaged in Section 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 as liability under the same does not cease to exist in the absence of dependency."

12. In the present case let alone the failure to prove that the daughters were dependent on the income of the deceased, they did not even try to prove this fact and they never came before the tribunal to prove their dependency.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Manjuri Bera v.
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., (2007) 10 SCC 643 has explained this issue very lucidly in the following terms:
13.

entities.text:
Manjuri Bera v.
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., (2007) 10 SCC 643
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are several factors which have to be noted.
The liability under Section 140 of the Act does not cease because there is absence of dependency.
The right to file a claim application has to be NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24671 7 MA-2448-2007 considered in the background of right to entitlement.
While assessing the quantum, the multiplier system is applied because of deprivation of dependency.
In other words, multiplier is a measure.
There are three stages while assessing the question of entitlement.
Firstly, the liability of the person who is liable and the person who is to indemnify the liability, if any.
Next is the quantification and Section 166 is primarily in the nature of recovery proceedings.
As noted above, liability in terms of Section 140 of the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency.
19. In the impugned judgment the High Court has correctly drawn a distinction between "right to apply for compensation" and "entitlement to compensation".
The High Court has rightly held that even a married daughter is a legal representative and she is certainly entitled to claim compensation.
It was further held, on the facts of the present case, that the married daughter was not dependent on her father.
She was living with her husband in her husband's house.

Therefore,
she was not entitled to claim statutory compensation.
According to the High Court, the claimant was not dependent on her father's income.
Hence, she was not entitled to claim compensation based on "no-fault liability".
20. In my opinion, "no-fault liability", envisaged in Section 140 of the said Act, is distinguishable from the rule of "strict liability".
In the former, the compensation amount is fixed.
It is Rs 50,000 in cases of death [Section 140(2)].
It is a statutory liability.
It is an amount which can be deducted from the final amount awarded by the Tribunal.

Since, the amount is a fixed amount/crystallised amount,
the same has to be considered as part of the estate of the deceased.
In the present case, the deceased was an earning member.
The statutory compensation could constitute part of his estate.
His legal representative, namely, his daughter has inherited his estate.
She was entitled to inherit his estate.

In the circumstances, she was entitled to receive compensation under "no-fault liability" in terms of National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Kalawati Bai & 6 Others on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22102234/
4 Section 140 of the said Act.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Kalawati Bai & 6 Others on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: My opinion is confined only to the "no-fault liability" under Section 140 of the said Act.
That section is a Code by itself within the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

13. As such it is hereby held that the two married daughters i.e claimants No.5 and 6 were not dependent on the income of the deceased consequently they were not entitled to for compensation quantifiable in terms of section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.
14. As regards the respondent No.1 i.e. the son of the deceased, it is seen from the proceedings of the case that the respondent no. 1 was living with the deceased Parwatibai.
There is no dispute about this fact.

15. It has also come on record undisputedly that the deceased was an NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:24671 8 MA-2448-2007 earning member of the family.
As such, this cannot be said by any stretch of imagination that the deceased Parwatibai being an earning member of the family was not contributing to the family for running the household.
As the deceased Parwati was living alongwith respondent No.1 Deepak.
As such in the considered view of this court only Deepak can be considered as only dependent of the deceased Parwati.

16. As far as the question of negligence is concerned, the initial report, documents regarding accident as well as the pleading clearly establish the negligence on the part of the driver/rider of the vehicle thus no interference is warranted in this behalf in the award of the tribunal.
As for the question of compensation to the person who was riding the bike i.e. respondent no. 1.
It may be incidental but this fact by itself will not exonerate the insurance company from its liability to pay compensation, once the accident was found proved.

17. In this view of the matter, the award of the claims tribunal is hereby modified to the extent that considering that there was only one dependent person on the deceased, deductions under the head of personal expenses is made at 50%.
Consequently, the compensation for loss of dependency comes to Rs.6,66,798/-.

As such the total compensation would now changed to Rs. 6,71,298 instead of Rs.
8,93,564/-.

As the respondents have already been paid Rs. 50,000/- for no fault liability in terms of section 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the respondent No.7 is entitled for payment of Rs.
6,71,298/-.

In the peculiar facts of this case the amount of interest is also modified from 9% to 6%
from the date of application before NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24671 9 MA-2448-2007 the claims tribunal.
18. With the aforesaid, the appeal of the insurance company is partly allowed.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Vatan National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Kalawati Bai & 6 Others on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22102234/
